title: Habib Goes Back-to-Back in Buckaroo Bowl II as Brucie Crashes the Party and the Commish Keeps the Basement Warm
dek: Kaushal's Habibsters ran the table from 11-3 to a second straight title, Ramon's Araleasers went from worst to the big game, and Ben Dover reported to last place for the second year in a row.
body: Last year, the Buckaroo Football League crowned its first champion. This year, it found out whether that was a fluke. It was not. Kaushal's Habibsters went 11-3, took the No. 1 seed again with 1,524.8 points, and won Buckaroo Bowl II, making Habibi the only name on the trophy through two seasons. Six managers drafted with fresh hope in the fall, and five of them spent the winter learning the same lesson.

The season opened with a warning shot from an unexpected place. Ramon's Araleasers, who finished 4-10 a year ago, dropped 166.58 points in week 1, the highest single-week score of the entire season. Brucie never quite reached that summit again, settling into a perfectly even 7-7, but it was enough for the 3 seed. For a guy who wasn't sure he even wanted to be here, he was suddenly playing like someone who had something to prove.

The cruelest stat line of 2024 belongs to Randy. The fumblers scored 1,595.1 points, the most in the league by a comfortable 70, and went 8-6 for the 2 seed. Then came the two-week semifinal against Araleasers, and the league's highest-powered offense picked the worst possible fortnight to go quiet, managing just 176.14 points to Ramon's 202.44. Randy leads the league in points and in reasons to complain, and he finished fourth. Also, for the second straight year, the BFL recorded zero trades, so nobody can say a deal ruined anything.

On the other side of the bracket, Alan snuck into the playoffs at 6-8 as the 4 seed, which is the fantasy equivalent of the bad guy slipping through the closing door at the last second. Philly's Team Pillbert put up a respectable 245.08 over two weeks, and it didn't matter one bit, because Habibsters answered with 296.96, the biggest playoff total of the year. Alan still walked away with third place, which in a six-team league means he gets to brag about beating Randy, and you know he will.

Buckaroo Bowl II was a demolition. Kaushal piled up 261.44 points over the two weeks, while Araleasers mustered 145.28, a 116-point margin and the kind of beatdown Habib usually reserves for watching SEC teams schedule cupcakes in September. The most telling number: Ramon's two-week Bowl total was lower than his single week 1 score. Somewhere, a Chicago-born Bills fan learned that turning your back on your hometown does not come with playoff luck. Still, from last place to the Buckaroo Bowl in one year is a heck of a glow-up, and Brucie earned every bit of runner-up.

Then there's the bottom of the ladder, where history repeated itself. Mekhi's Dawgs and Sonny's Ben Dover both went 5-9, but Ben Dover scored a league-low 1,304.3 points and posted the season's single worst week, a 44.1 in week 12 that looked more like a bye-week roster than a lineup. Kai took fifth, and Sonny took the basement for the second straight season. Two years, two last places for the commissioner, which is either a cautionary tale or the opening act of a comeback story nobody saw coming.

So the record book now reads: Buckaroo Bowl II, Habibsters, champion; Ben Dover, last place. Same top, same bottom, entirely new chaos in the middle. Kaushal is the league's first dynasty, Ramon proved the worst can climb, Randy has the points to prove he was robbed, and Sonny has one more offseason to figure out how to go from last to anything else. Two years down. Somebody has to stop Habib eventually, right?
